ordinary_release.wasm_identity_note: Executable bytes changed by relocation. The preserved b93 and refreshed a73 Wasm artifacts have equal length but differ in SHA-256 because SDL CMake stamps the project revision into SDL_REVISION. The exact 19-byte literal occurs once in each DATA segment set: SDL-3.4.10-b93b7bd at memory address 225226 and SDL-3.4.10-a73eac5 at 302238. After removing each exact literal, 517 u32le and 27 u24le data pointer fields each shift by -19; replacing the new fields with the old values makes all 4,233 DATA segment payloads byte-for-byte equal. LLVM disassembly reports identical instruction addresses and mnemonics, with 5,124 changed operands: 5,123 address immediates shift by -19 and the remaining i32.const in SDL_InitSubSystem changes from 225226 to 302238. No browser capture used the refreshed Wasm; the successful capture remains attributed only to b93.

wasm_delta_analysis.interpretation: Executable CODE bytes changed in address immediates. Every disassembled opcode mnemonic and instruction offset is unchanged. Current generated SDL revision literal is the only non-pointer DATA payload content difference: the exact 19-byte old/new literal is removed from its respective data segment, after which all remaining DATA differences are 517 u32le and 27 u24le fields whose encoded values each shift by -19. The 77,012 i32.const delta is the memory address of the moved literal. This explains the Wasm delta; it does not make the refreshed Wasm the producer of the historical browser capture, which remains tied to b93.
